title: Skip Links & Navigation Efficiency 🏃
description: Design skip navigation links, landmark‑based shortcuts, and efficient keyboard routes.

slides.title: The Problem: Repetitive Navigation 🌀
slides.content:
Many pages have extensive navigation bars, search fields, and sidebars before the main content. A keyboard user must tab through all of these on **every single page** to reach the main content.

Enter the **skip navigation link** – a link that jumps directly to the main content, bypassing all that repetition.

It's typically the very first focusable element on the page, often visually hidden until focused.

quizData.question: Who benefits most from a skip navigation link?

options.text: Keyboard users who must tab through every menu item
Screen reader users who only listen

quizData.explanation: Keyboard and screen reader users use skip links to avoid repetitive navigation.

slides.title: How to Build a Skip Link 🔧
Complete Skip Link HTML/CSS
slides.codeSnippet:
Skip to main content
...
.skip-to-main { position: absolute; left: -999px; top: auto; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; } .skip-to-main:focus { left: 0; top: 0; width: auto; height: auto; padding: 1em; background: black; color: white; text-align: center; }

quizData.question: Why must the target `<main>` have `tabindex="-1"` when used with a skip link?

options.text: To make it focusable so it can receive focus from the skip link
To hide it from screen readers

quizData.explanation: `<main>` is not natively focusable; `tabindex="-1"` allows it to receive programmatic focus without being in the tab order.

slides.title: Beyond Skip Links: Landmark Navigation 🗺️
slides.content:
Screen reader users can already navigate by landmarks (see Chapter 3). But keyboard‑only sighted users need skip links. For heavy‑duty web apps, consider:

- **Multiple skip links**: "Skip to main", "Skip to search", "Skip to footer".
- **Accesskeys**: (deprecated, avoid – they conflict with assistive tech).
- **Keyboard shortcuts** (custom, with a method to disable/reassign).

Always keep it simple: a good skip link + logical DOM order covers 95% of needs.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Test your skip link
Turn on your screen reader, load the page, press Tab. The first thing you should hear is 'Skip to main content, link'. Press Enter – focus should move to the main content.
